title: Deployment readiness: quantization scan and cosine audit for embedding fleets
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Run a production-ready validation and ops checklist for INT8/FP16 quant profiles applied to our embedding models and implement a nightly cosine-similarity audit that gates rollouts. The goal is to ensure any quantized model variant meets defined similarity budgets across key corpora and signal slices before being promoted to Dedicated and Hosted fleets.
background: Recent internal experiments show variable cosine similarity degradation for some INT8 transforms on long-tail corpora. We need a standardized calibration workflow plus an automated drift detector with per-corpus adaptive thresholds, and an operational rollback gate integrated with the Console rollout APIs.
proposal: 1) Create a deterministic calibration pipeline that emits per-layer scaling stats, per-token quantization error histograms, and a canonical similarity snapshot set. 2) Build a nightly scanner that computes cosine deltas vs baseline snapshots per corpus and per-slice, applies a calibrated threshold, and opens a ticket + triggers canary rollback if regressions exceed tolerance. 3) Add a lightweight local re-calibration step for problematic models: layer-wise bias correction and re-scaling before rollout.
calibration_workflow: Collect representative calibration corpora per-customer segment (web docs, short queries, long-form) with anchors sampled deterministically
Run per-layer range collection using 32-bit reference runs on validation shard (batch-size controlled to mimic production P99 path)
Compute layerwise scale/zero params for INT8 and FP16 profiles; export a profile artifact (profile-id, sha, metadata)
Produce a canonical embedding snapshot (N=20k anchors) with reference float32 outputs and attach corpus metadata
Store calibration artifacts in GCS (gcs://redwood-quant/profiles/{profile-id}) and register in profiles index for auditability
validation_plan: Run similarity checks for each candidate quant profile against the canonical snapshot using cosine similarity
Compute distributional deltas (mean, median, 90/95/99 percentiles) and a per-anchor failure rate (below 0.95 sim)
Evaluate downstream impact via a small reranking eval harness and embedding nearest-neighbor recall on held-out queries
Run sensitivity sweeps for batch-size and sequence-length to detect non-linear degradation patterns
Publish a validation report artifact with PR linking and a human-readable pass/fail verdict
acceptance_criteria: Mean cosine delta across all corpora <= 0.005 and 95th percentile delta <= 0.02 OR documented justification signed off by PM
No corpus shows >0.5% anchors with similarity under 0.92 compared to float baseline without mitigation
Nightly scanner implemented and raising alerts in PagerDuty for sustained breaches (>=3 consecutive nightly failures)
Rollout gating wired: failing profile prevents canary promotion in Console and creates rollback runbook link
Artifacts uploaded and linked (profile, snapshot, validation report) for each candidate build
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed comparing FP16 vs INT8 for model-v3 on web-docs corpus. INT8 shows heavier tail degradation on long-form anchors.
2026-03-04: Prototype calibration pipeline (calib-runner v0.1) can emit per-layer histograms and profile artifacts. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/calibration/pull/182
2026-03-06: Nightly scanner prototype finished; computes cosine deltas and writes summary rows to bigquery table redwood.quant_cosine_audit. Dashboard draft: grafana/r/quant-nightly-audit
2026-03-09: Added adaptive per-corpus thresholds derived from baseline variance; updated acceptance criteria to use mean+3*sigma guardrail
2026-03-10: Integration work with Console rollout API started (Console PR under review). Blocking item: need secure storage for profile artifacts across Private customers (see risk below)
risks_mitigation: Risk: Some customers' private corpora are too small to form stable baselines. Mitigation: fallback to a model-level baseline plus synthetic augmentation and conservative thresholds
Risk: Nightly jobs could produce false positives when upstream data drift occurs. Mitigation: correlate cosine drops with corpus-stats change and require 3-night persistence before auto-rollback
Risk: Profile artifact integrity in Private deployments. Mitigation: add signed metadata and optional KMS encryption for profile blobs
Risk: CPU/GPU cost of running reference float runs at scale. Mitigation: sample anchors intelligently and use stratified sampling to preserve tail coverage
